definitions.explanation: A person one works with, emphasizing the sense of companionship and shared effort rather than formal organizational hierarchy.

examples.japanese: {仕事仲間|しごとなかま}と{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I had lunch with my work colleagues.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はただの{仕事仲間|しごとなかま}ではなく、{親友|しんゆう}だ。
examples.english: He's not just a work colleague — he's a close friend.

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}に{仕事仲間|しごとなかま}と{飲|の}みに{行|い}くことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: I often go out drinking with my coworkers on weekends.

notes:
Carries a warmer, more personal tone than {同僚|どうりょう} (colleague). {仲間|なかま} implies camaraderie and a sense of being on the same team, so {仕事仲間|しごとなかま} suggests people you get along with at work, not merely people who happen to work at the same place.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事仲間|しごとなかま}と{飲|の}みに{行|い}く: to go drinking with coworkers
- {仕事仲間|しごとなかま}に{恵|めぐ}まれる: to be blessed with good colleagues
- {大切|たいせつ}な{仕事仲間|しごとなかま}: valued coworkers

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {同僚|どうりょう}: colleague — more formal and neutral; no implication of personal closeness
- {職場|しょくば}の{人|ひと}: people at one's workplace — general, no warmth implied
- {同期|どうき}: someone who joined the company in the same year — specific to hiring cohort
